capabilities: Read notes or selections aloud using the operating system's voices
Export notes or selections as WAV files with a downloadable Piper voice
Transcribe audio files in the vault into new notes
Prepare speech-ready text by skipping frontmatter, code blocks, embeds and comments
Handle transcription and spoken-word files on iOS via an Apple Shortcut
disambiguation: Not an audio player or recorder; it turns written notes into spoken audio and audio files into text transcripts.
extras: Downloads nothing until the user enables WAV export and clicks Download; voice files are checksum-verified and stored outside the vault. Transcription accepts only local addresses (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]). Full documentation, including troubleshooting, is hosted externally.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to read notes aloud or turn notes into audio files, and typical TTS services require cloud access and accounts.

relations.evidence: English (Piper, LJSpeech) or German (Piper, Thorsten), medium quality, switchable in the settings
The companion program is audio-ui — speech recognition (Parakeet) running locally on Apple Silicon
on iOS/iPadOS, an Apple Shortcut transcribes audio files and turns text into a spoken-word file

requires.name: companion program audio-ui (local speech recognition) for transcription on desktop

summary: Text-to-speech plugin that reads notes aloud with system voices, exports them as WAV files locally, and transcribes audio files into notes.
